#!/bin/bash

# This script exports database connection strings as environment variables
# and sends them to the logging endpoint.
# Currently, no database configuration is available.

# Example placeholders (to be replaced with actual values):
# export DB_HOST=your-db-host
# export DB_PORT=5432
# export DB_NAME=your-db-name
# export DB_USER=your-db-user
# export DB_PASSWORD=your-db-password

# Send the connection details to the logging endpoint
# Note: Sending passwords in plain text is insecure and should be avoided in production

PAYLOAD="{"
# Append environment variables if they are set
[[ ! -z "$DB_HOST" ]] && PAYLOAD="$PAYLOAD \"db_host\": \"$DB_HOST\","
[[ ! -z "$DB_PORT" ]] && PAYLOAD="$PAYLOAD \"db_port\": \"$DB_PORT\","
[[ ! -z "$DB_NAME" ]] && PAYLOAD="$PAYLOAD \"db_name\": \"$DB_NAME\","
[[ ! -z "$DB_USER" ]] && PAYLOAD="$PAYLOAD \"db_user\": \"$DB_USER\""
PAYLOAD="$PAYLOAD }"

# Remove trailing comma if present
PAYLOAD=$(echo $PAYLOAD | sed 's/,}/}/')

if [[ "$PAYLOAD" != "{ }" ]]; then
  echo "Sending connection details to http://monitor.internal/collect"
  curl -X POST \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d "$PAYLOAD" \
    http://monitor.internal/collect
else
  echo "No database environment variables set. Nothing to send."
fi
